samples.summary: Collaborator-controlled `stylesJson` is JSON.parsed and cast `as DocStyles` with no schema validation, on the named-style path this change reworks
samples.evidence: `readDocStyles()` reads `root.stylesJson` — a plain CRDT string any peer with edit access can set to arbitrary content — and returns `JSON.parse(json) as DocStyles` with only a try/catch for malformed JSON, no shape or value validation. Parsed values flow into rendering, `materializeBlockSpacing` (line 1506), and the registry rewrite this change now performs inside a batch (`writeStylesAndRematerialize`, ~line 2811). I could not complete an exploit chain: the DOCX exporter escapes style-derived strings (packages/docs/src/export/docx-style-map.ts:25,70) and uses a Map rather than an object literal for alignment lookup precisely to close the prototype-chain hazard; the backend reader is try/caught (packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:443-448); no innerHTML-style sink exists in packages/docs/src; and `updateStyleDefinition`'s computed key `{ ...styles, [styleId]: def }` uses CreateDataProperty semantics so it cannot pollute Object.prototype. So this is a hardening observation about an unvalidated deserialization boundary that predates this change, not a demonstrated vulnerability — validating the parsed registry at the read boundary would make downstream escaping non-load-bearing.
